audit.title: Deprecation of Chainlink Data Streams
audit.summary: This is a reference page listing which Chainlink Data Streams feeds are scheduled for deprecation, with feed IDs, shutdown dates, and per-stream report schemas. Its biggest strength is dense, specific data (feed IDs, schema versions, decimals, dates) wrapped in valid `TechArticle`/`BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD. Its biggest weakness is that the high-value facts live inside two enormous 1,200-word tables with no answer-first summary, no explanation of *what deprecation means for a user*, and no per-stream/query-phrased anchors — so an engine asked "is the ETH/USDT Data Stream being deprecated and when?" has no liftable sentence and a hard-to-chunk table to parse instead. The page is factually rich but structurally under-optimized for retrieval and synthesis.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first summary block above the first table
recommendations.where: Immediately after the intro, before "Mainnet Deprecating Streams."
recommendations.issue: "A list of Data Streams feeds designated for deprecation... can be found below."
recommendations.change: Add a self-contained lead: "As of September 2026, N mainnet and M testnet Chainlink Data Streams feeds are scheduled for deprecation, with shutdown dates ranging from December 2025 to September 2026. After a feed's shutdown date, it stops producing verifiable reports and consumers must migrate to an active stream." Include the count and date range.
recommendations.why: Gives engines one liftable sentence that answers the core query; without it, answers must be synthesized from an unchunkable table and often fail.

recommendations.title: Define what deprecation means and what users must do
recommendations.where: New short H2 "What happens when a Data Stream is deprecated?"
recommendations.issue: Page states feeds "may be scheduled for deprecation" but never says what breaks or the required action.
recommendations.change: 2–3 sentences: what stops on the shutdown date, whether reports still verify, and the migration path (link to selecting-data-streams). Include the recommended action explicitly.
recommendations.why: Covers the "what should I do" intent that the current page silently drops; wins symptom queries like "my Chainlink stream stopped updating."

recommendations.title: Make each stream individually retrievable
recommendations.issue: Two ~1,200-word single-table sections with repeated nested schema tables; no per-stream anchor.
recommendations.change: Either add an H3 per stream (e.g. "### ETH/USDT (Mainnet) — deprecating August 19th, 2026") or, at minimum, a compact top-level summary table (Stream | Network | Shutdown date | Feed ID | Schema) with the verbose schema field tables collapsed/linked out rather than inlined per row.
recommendations.why: Creates clean chunk boundaries and named anchors so "is BNB/USDT being deprecated" retrieves a coherent unit instead of a 1k-word blob.

recommendations.title: Normalize date formats
recommendations.issue: "August 19th, 2026" vs "February 2026" vs "December 2025" — mixed precision and format.
recommendations.change: Use ISO-style consistent dates (`2026-08-19`; for month-only, `2026-02`). Note explicitly where only a month is committed.
recommendations.why: Consistent, parseable dates let agents extract and compare shutdown schedules reliably.

recommendations.title: Fix freshness and entity metadata
recommendations.issue: `dateModified` identical to `datePublished`; `about[]` is the auto-template "Content about deprecation/chainlink/data/streams."
recommendations.change: Stamp `dateModified` on each real edit (this list changes frequently — freshness is a genuine trust signal here). Replace the split `about` entries with a single real entity, e.g. `{"@type":"Thing","name":"Chainlink Data Streams"}`.
recommendations.why: Accurate freshness and entity signals raise E-E-A-T and entity resolution; a deprecation page especially benefits from a credible last-updated date.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/FAQ heading pair
recommendations.issue: No coverage of how devs phrase the problem ("how do I know if my stream is deprecated," "where do I get deprecation notifications").
recommendations.change: Short FAQ: "How am I notified of Data Streams deprecations?" (point to the Discord `data-feeds-user-notifications` channel already linked) and "How do I check if a specific feed ID is deprecated?"
recommendations.why: Headings phrased as the exact questions win retrieval that concept-titled tables miss.

antiPatterns: **Walls of undifferentiated tabular content** — two sections, each a single 1,200-word table with schema sub-tables repeated verbatim per stream; poor chunk boundaries.
**Stale/ambiguous freshness signal** — `dateModified` equals `datePublished` on a page that changes as streams are added.
**Auto-template entity metadata** — `about[]` fragments the real entity ("Data Streams") into four generic Things.
No keyword stuffing or marketing fluff detected.
offPageNotes: Site-level: ensure this page is reachable from the Data Streams hub and `selecting-data-streams` page so it is discoverable as the canonical deprecation authority.
Consider an `llms.txt` entry pointing engines to this as the authoritative deprecation schedule.
CLI note: raw `<head>` was provided and parsed; freshness cadence is the main site-level trust lever for this specific page type.
